name: Array Traversal
description: Visit each element in order using a loop.
exampleJava: for (int i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) { sum += arr[i]; }
commonMistakes: Using the wrong loop boundary
Skipping the first or last element

name: Matrix Traversal
description: Visit every cell of a 2D grid using nested loops while tracking row and column boundaries correctly.
exampleJava: for (int row = 0; row < matrix.length; row++) for (int col = 0; col < matrix[row].length; col++) total += matrix[row][col];
commonMistakes: Mixing up row count and column count
Using matrix.length for both loop bounds

name: Boundary Traversal
description: Walk the outer ring or a specific layer of a matrix without double-counting corners or revisiting cells.
exampleJava: for (int col = left; col <= right; col++) sum += matrix[top][col];
commonMistakes: Double-counting corners
Traversing bottom or left edges when the layer has collapsed

name: Min and Max in Array
description: Track the best value seen so far while scanning the array once.
exampleJava: int best = arr[0]; for (int value : arr) best = Math.max(best, value);
commonMistakes: Initializing from 0 when array can contain negatives
Forgetting to handle a single-element array

name: Sorted Check
description: Compare each element with the next one to verify ordering.
exampleJava: for (int i = 1; i < arr.length; i++) if (arr[i] < arr[i - 1]) return false;
commonMistakes: Using > instead of < for ascending checks
Not handling arrays of length 0 or 1

name: Reverse Array
description: Swap elements from both ends until pointers meet.
exampleJava: while (left < right) { int t = arr[left]; arr[left++] = arr[right]; arr[right--] = t; }
commonMistakes: Not moving both pointers
Using extra memory when in-place reversal is expected

name: Second Largest
description: Track the largest and second largest values in one pass.
exampleJava: if (x > first) { second = first; first = x; } else if (x > second && x != first) { second = x; }
commonMistakes: Not handling duplicates carefully
Using sorting for a problem that expects one pass

name: Frequency Counting
description: Count how many times each value appears using a map or count array.
exampleJava: map.put(x, map.getOrDefault(x, 0) + 1);
commonMistakes: Forgetting to initialize missing counts
Using nested loops unnecessarily

name: Prefix Sum
description: Precompute running sums so range-sum queries become fast.
exampleJava: prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + arr[i];
commonMistakes: Off-by-one errors in prefix indexing
Forgetting the extra 0 at the front

name: Kadane Algorithm
description: Track the best subarray ending at each index.
exampleJava: current = Math.max(arr[i], current + arr[i]); best = Math.max(best, current);
commonMistakes: Resetting to 0 incorrectly when all values are negative
Confusing current sum and best sum

name: Two Pointers
description: Maintain two moving indices to transform or scan an array efficiently.
exampleJava: while (left < right) { ... left++; right--; }
commonMistakes: Moving only one pointer
Breaking sorted-array assumptions

name: In-place Array Update
description: Modify the same array without allocating another full answer array.
exampleJava: nums[write] = nums[read];
commonMistakes: Overwriting values too early
Returning the wrong final length

name: Sliding Window
description: Grow and shrink a window while tracking the answer incrementally.
exampleJava: sum += arr[right]; while (sum > k) sum -= arr[left++];
commonMistakes: Forgetting to shrink the window
Using this trick on arrays with negative numbers when it does not apply

name: Opposite-End Pointers
description: Start one pointer at each end and decide which side to move based on the current constraint or score.
exampleJava: while (left < right) { area = Math.max(area, Math.min(h[left], h[right]) * (right - left)); if (h[left] < h[right]) left++; else right--; }
commonMistakes: Moving the taller side when the shorter side limits the answer
Forgetting to update the answer before moving a pointer

name: Partition Two Pointers
description: Use read and write regions to compact, partition, or overwrite an array in place.
exampleJava: for (int read = 0; read < nums.length; read++) if (nums[read] != 0) nums[write++] = nums[read];
commonMistakes: Overwriting values before they are processed
Returning or printing the wrong effective prefix length

name: Fixed-Size Window
description: Keep exactly k elements in the window and update the answer as the window slides one step at a time.
exampleJava: sum += nums[i]; if (i >= k) sum -= nums[i - k]; if (i >= k - 1) best = Math.max(best, sum);
commonMistakes: Using the answer before the first full window forms
Removing the outgoing element too early or too late

name: Variable-Size Window
description: Expand and shrink the window based on a condition instead of a fixed length.
exampleJava: for (int right = 0; right < nums.length; right++) { sum += nums[right]; while (sum > target) sum -= nums[left++]; }
commonMistakes: Shrinking only once when repeated shrinking is needed
Applying the positive-only trick to arrays with negatives

name: Window Auxiliary Structure
description: Pair the sliding window with a queue, deque, or list of candidates when the raw window sum is not enough.
exampleJava: while (!deque.isEmpty() && deque.peekFirst() <= i - k) deque.pollFirst();
commonMistakes: Forgetting to evict expired indices
Storing values when indices are needed to detect expiry

name: Prefix-Suffix Product
description: Accumulate products from the left and right to answer each index without division.
exampleJava: answer[i] = prefix[i] * suffix[i];
commonMistakes: Using division despite zero handling issues
Misaligning prefix and suffix arrays by one index

name: Prefix Balance
description: Compare the accumulated contribution on the left and right side of each index to find pivots and equilibrium points.
exampleJava: if (leftSum == totalSum - leftSum - nums[i]) return i;
commonMistakes: Including the current element in both sides
Updating leftSum in the wrong order

name: Prefix Modulo
description: Track prefix sums modulo k so matching remainders reveal divisible subarrays.
exampleJava: int mod = ((prefix % k) + k) % k; answer += freq.getOrDefault(mod, 0);
commonMistakes: Forgetting to normalize negative remainders
Not seeding remainder 0 with frequency 1

name: Stock Profit Scan
description: Track the minimum buy price so far and the best profit so far.
exampleJava: minPrice = Math.min(minPrice, price); best = Math.max(best, price - minPrice);
commonMistakes: Buying after selling in the scan logic
Resetting the minimum incorrectly
